summary: PULSO ("the pulse of the Earth") is a trend detective that tells you which Earth-system trends to trust. Ask a question in plain language (English or Spanish) and PULSO pulls NASA data (POWER: MERRA-2, GPM/IMERG, CERES), removes seasonality, runs a seasonal Mann-Kendall test with Sen's slope and 95% intervals, maps neighboring regions to catch opposite trends, and traces the "domino effect" between rain, soil moisture, evaporation and heat. Its key idea is the Trust Seal: every trend must survive six tests - significance, record length, stability, robustness to extreme events, confirmation by a second independent source (TerraClimate) and a physics audit. A Change Atlas scans 1,842 cells x 10 variables with false-discovery control. Our case study is the 2023-24 Panama Canal water crisis: heat and soil stress are confirmed, and Sentinel-1 radar shows Gatun Lake's water surface shrank modestly and then recovered. It matters because water decisions should rest on trends that survive scrutiny, not on artifacts. It works on phones and needs no login.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

PULSO turns a plain-language question ("Is the Panama Canal watershed drying out?") into a tested answer. It downloads NASA POWER series (MERRA-2, GPM/IMERG, CERES), removes the seasonal cycle and applies a seasonal Mann-Kendall test with Sen's slope and 95% confidence intervals. It then maps neighboring cells to detect opposite trends, finds lagged correlations (the "domino effect") between rain, soil moisture, evaporation, clouds and heat, and separates extreme events from permanent change.

THE TRUST SEAL (our main idea)

Most tools draw a trend line. PULSO tests it with six independent checks: significance, record length, stability across both halves of the record, robustness when extreme months are removed, confirmation by a second independent source (TerraClimate, 4 km) and a physics audit (Clausius-Clapeyron, water balance, radiation). The result is HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW confidence. Example: Panama heat is HIGH (about +0.2 C/decade in both sources), while northern Venezuela's +1.12 C/decade in MERRA-2 versus +0.11 in TerraClimate is LOW, a likely reanalysis artifact.

CHANGE ATLAS

An automatic global scan of 1,842 cells x 10 variables (1990-2025) with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery control: 8,770 of 14,985 trends survive. The physics auditor flags 251 cells (13.6%) with physical inconsistencies. It is a 5-degree sample, not full coverage.

CASE STUDY: PANAMA CANAL 2023-24

Heat was +2.07 standard deviations above normal during the crisis (peak +3.42) and root-zone soil moisture was -0.99 (peak -3.06). Sentinel-1 radar (162 scenes, one fixed orbit) shows Gatun Lake's water surface 1.4% below baseline during the crisis versus +0.4% in normal months (about 5.6 km2, p about 9e-6), recovering in 2025. The effect is small because the shores are steep, so we present it as supporting evidence. Rain in the basin was near normal on average. USGS earthquakes are included only as infrastructure-risk context.

IMPACT

Water managers, journalists and students can see not only what is changing but how much to trust it. PULSO is bilingual (Spanish/English), works on phones, needs no login and is publicly hosted.

HOW WE BUILT IT

Python, FastAPI, NumPy/SciPy (every number comes from deterministic code; the AI only writes explanations), Leaflet, Plotly, xarray/zarr, Microsoft Planetary Computer and Azure App Service. Code and the logo were created with AI assistance (see the AI disclosure).

LIMITS

5-degree Atlas sample; TerraClimate verification covers 1990-2021; MERRA-2 cells are about 50 km wide; correlation is not causation.
